text: Aoife was chopping green onions when she remembered the big match. She wiped her hands on a towel and said, "Excuse me, could you please read me the football results from last night? I have been in the kitchen all day, and I would like to know how my team did before my family gets home." The speaker said it would deliver the scores right away. It read out three results in a calm voice. Her team had won two to one. Aoife smiled and felt her whole body relax. "Thank you," she said. Then she asked it to read the headlines about the local market too, and the assistant did. She kept on cooking while the news played.

Ravi, a grandfather, was cold in bed on Saturday night. The garden outside looked frozen. He told the phone, "Wake me at seven on Sunday, and please don't let me stay in bed any later than that." The phone set an alarm for seven in the morning on Sunday and said it was ready. Then Ravi asked, "How long will I sleep if I go to bed now?" It was ten o'clock. The phone said that if he slept until seven, he would get nine hours. Ravi nodded. He asked it to play a quiet rain sound for thirty-one minutes. The phone started the sound, and Ravi closed his eyes.

Someone who is careful about their house wants to know if the front door is locked, and they ask from their phone.
Is the front door locked?
front door locked?
Did I lock up?
I think I forgot the door, can you check it?
I'm a bit worried, is the door shut and locked?
Check the lock on the front door for me.
I earn more when I get to work early, so tell me quickly if the front door is locked.
Could you please tell me whether I locked the front door when I left? I am too far away to go back, and I won't be able to relax until I know.

Fatou was packing lunches when her phone buzzed. She said, "Read me the top news about the bank, please. I need to hear about the loan rates." The assistant started to give her the business headlines. "No, wait," said Fatou. "Not the bank. I mean the city council news." It was urgent, because the council was voting on the school bus routes that morning. The assistant stopped, changed the topic, and read three headlines from the local news. One of them said the vote would be at ten. Fatou listened while she zipped the lunch bags and called the kids to the door.

Ruta burned her hand on the stove. She was not good with phones, but she remembered the speaker on the shelf. "Hey assistant, burn help!" she said. The speaker told her to hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes. It said not to use ice. Ruta was about to grab a frozen bag from the freezer, but she stopped. She bathed her hand in the cool water from the tap instead. After a while she asked, "Next step?" The speaker said to cover the burn loosely with a clean cloth, and to call a doctor if it blistered badly. Ruta did as it said, and her hand felt much better.

Someone wants to join a work call from their pricey new laptop.
Join my call.
Get me into the meeting.
Open the team call.
Is the nine o'clock meeting live yet? Put me in.
I'm about to lock up the office, can you start the call for me?
Hey, hop on the standup for me, I'm holding a carton of milk and can't reach the keys.
Could you please join the video meeting with my manager? I'm running late, I still have to lock my bike, and I don't want to miss the start.
Would you mind connecting me to the planning call? My hands are full and I'd like to listen in while I walk to the station.

A bike route is the path you ride from one place to another. Years ago, people drew their routes on paper with a pencil. Now an assistant can design a route for you in a few seconds. People change a few things about it: how far they want to ride, how fast they want to go, and whether they like flat roads or hills. They say things like "Make it shorter," "Keep it under twenty kilometers," or "Find me a flat way to the lake." On a crispy autumn morning, many riders ask for a long route. On a hot day, they ask for a short one with shade.

Someone wants the calendar to update because a meeting has to move to a later time.
Move my meeting later.
Push the three o'clock to four.
Can you try to shift my call with Dana to tomorrow?
I won't be out of the dentist by three.
The automatic reminder still says three, but the meeting is at five now, can you fix it?
Any chance you could slide the team meeting back by an hour?
I'm stuck in traffic and I'm going to miss my two o'clock.
Would you please move my lunch with Omar to Friday? Something came up at work, and I would like to let him know as soon as possible.

name: check_purifier_filter
does: Checks if a purifier's filter is dirty and tells you whether it just needs a wipe or the whole filter needs to be replaced.
inputs: which purifier or room, like the bedroom one or the one you borrowed from a neighbor
people say:
- Is my purifier filter dirty?
- The air smells stale, does the filter need changing?
- Can the filter be cleaned or do I need a new one?
- Why is the purifier so loud lately?
- When did I last change the filter in the bedroom?

Person: Put a new task on my list for tomorrow.
Assistant: Okay. What is the task?
Person: Call the shop about the wifi box.
Assistant: Added: call the shop about the wifi box, for tomorrow. Anything else?
Person: Wait, I meant Thursday, not tomorrow. And I also need to get bread.
Assistant: Done. The wifi call is moved to Thursday. Should I put get bread on the same day?
Person: No, today. I have too many things left on the list already.
Assistant: Okay, get bread is on today's list. You have six tasks left today. Do you want to hear them?
Person: Not now, thank you.

name: block_free_time
does: Reserves a single block of time in your calendar, such as time to listen to an audiobook, until you lift it.
inputs: the day, the start and end times, and a short label
people say:
- Keep Friday afternoon free for me.
- Don't let anyone book me between two and four.
- I need an hour to myself tomorrow morning.
- Block off my lunch break every day.
- Mark me as busy on Monday.

Person: I'm new to this city and I want to invite some neighbors for a holiday dinner. Can you set a reminder?
Assistant: Happy to. What should the reminder say, and when?
Person: Wash the good plates on Friday at five.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on Friday at five to wash the good plates. Do you want help with the menu?
Person: Yes. Everyone will be hungry, so something big. Can you also call my neighbors to invite them?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't make phone calls. I can write a short invitation for you to send, though.
Person: Yes please, with a toast at the end.
Assistant: Dinner at my place on Saturday at six. Come hungry, and let's raise a toast to the new year!

Someone wants the heating turned up.
Turn up the heat.
Heating on, please.
It's cold in here.
Make the living room warmer.
Warm up the bedroom fast, I'm going to bed soon.
My feet are freezing, can you put the radiators on?
Could you please turn the heating up to twenty-two degrees in the living room? We are about to sit down with a big melon and some tea, and my grandmother's knees hurt when the room is cold.
Would you mind switching on the heater in the hallway? The baby is sleeping nearby and I don't want her to get chilly.

name: check_home_for_leaks
does: Checks the water meter and pipes for a leak and sends you a message with what it found, so the home stays dry and cozy.
inputs: which room or pipe to check, and where to send the message
people say:
- Is water leaking anywhere at home?
- The water bill is huge, something must be running.
- I'm on the bus, can you tell me if the pipes are okay?
- There's a wet spot under the sink.
- I hear dripping inside the wall.
- Did the washing machine leave a puddle?

Ravi had borrowed his sister's pasta recipe, and now steam was fogging up the kitchen window. His hands were covered in flour, and his phone sat on a clean towel. "Set a timer for ten minutes and read me the next step," he said. The phone started the timer and read out the step: stir the sauce and add a pinch of salt. Ravi stirred the pot, tasted it, and added the salt. When the timer rang, the phone read the last step, and he drained the pasta. His kids sat down at the table, and they said it was the best pasta he had ever made.

Martha was cooking soup for her uncle. He was outside mowing the lawn, and he would be hungry soon. She stirred the pot and asked her speaker, "Time left?" The speaker said there were eleven minutes left on the timer. Martha cut some bread and set the table. Then she asked, "Final step?" The speaker read it out: add fresh parsley, then turn off the heat. Martha did that and smiled. When her uncle came in, wiping his hands, the soup was hot and the table was ready. He said it smelled wonderful.

name: small_injury_steps
does: Reads out the steps to treat a small injury, such as a scrape or a burn, and tells you when to call a doctor.
inputs: what kind of injury it is and where on the body
people say:
- I fell off my scooter and scraped my knee.
- My finger is bleeding, what do I do?
- How do I treat a burn from the oven?
- My sister's ankle is swollen after a fall.
- Should I keep the bandage wet or dry?
- What now? He cut his hand.

Xiu burned the rice, and the kitchen filled with smoke. She opened a window, then picked up her phone. She was not good with apps, so she typed fast: "ordr my usual from the noodle place". The assistant looked at her past orders and said her usual was two noodle soups and a tea. It asked if that was right. Xiu typed "yes". The assistant placed the order and said it would come in thirty minutes. Xiu sat on the sofa to rest until the doorbell rang, and dinner was saved.

Meera was a student, and money was tight. She was walking to the post office to ship a parcel to her mother when she asked her phone, "Can you find a cheap haircut near campus? I want to pay less than I did last time." The assistant found a top-rated barber that cost half as much as her old salon, about fifteen dollars. It said there was a free slot on Thursday at four. "Book it," said Meera. The assistant booked the slot and added it to her calendar. Meera smiled, dropped off the parcel, and walked home.

Oscar was in a hurry. The pasta would cook for ten minutes, and he wanted to read while he waited. He said to his tablet, "Open my book and tell me how many pages are left in this chapter." The tablet opened the book at his bookmark and said five pages were left, about three minutes of reading. That was less than half the time the pasta needed. Oscar read fast, and his body relaxed for the first time that day. He was happy to finish the chapter before the pasta was done. "Put a bookmark here," he said, and the tablet did.

Someone wants to know which bin to sort an item into.
Which bin does this go in?
Where does a broken toaster go?
Can I recycle this?
I don't know how to sort my trash.
It's bitter cold out and I don't want to drag the wrong bin to the street.
The kitchen is full of cardboard and I have no idea where it goes.
I have a pile of old glass jars, what do I do with them?
Could you please tell me whether a plastic tub that held butter goes in the recycling or the regular trash? I would like to do it properly.

Nimal was driving to the depot when his work call started. He was bored of long meetings, and he had a rule not to look at screens while driving. "Join my nine o'clock meeting," he said to the car assistant, "but don't turn on my camera and don't read me the chat." The assistant joined by audio only, with the camera off. Nimal heard his boss talk about next week's schedule. When the call ended, he asked the assistant to remind him to book his workout for the evening. The assistant said it would, and Nimal drove on.

Roya was studying in her room when the afternoon sun hit her screen. Her fish tank sat in the bright light too. She said, "Lower the blinds on the desk window and open the curtains by the bed." The blinds went down and the curtains slid open. Now the room was calm and the tank was in the shade. Her cat tried to jump onto the desk, so Roya added, "Play some quiet music." The assistant started her personal study playlist. Roya went back to her notes and read for another hour.

Aarav unlocked his car and sat down. He had a long drive ahead and wanted to be safe, so he checked the road first. He typed to the car assistant in a hurry: "put on the trafic news on 94 fm". The assistant tuned the radio to 94 FM, and the traffic report came on. A road was closed on his usual way. Then a local band played a song, and Aarav asked the assistant to keep that station on. It did, and he took a different road to work.

Baraka owned a small shop near the forest road. The air filter in the back was full of dust, and the deep sink was blocked too. He said to his phone, "Find someone to fix my air filter and book them for Tuesday." The phone found a repair man named Lutalo who could come at ten in the morning, and it booked the slot. Baraka then said, "Remind me to lift the boxes off the floor tonight. There are fifty of them." The phone set a reminder for six in the evening, and Baraka went back to serving his customers.

After a long day in the garden, Imran went to bed early. His tie was ready on the chair for the flower market meeting in the morning. He did not want to forget the time, so he said, "Wake me at six, but not with the loud alarm. I don't want to scare the cat." The assistant set an alarm for six with a soft bird sound. Imran also asked it to turn off the electric blanket after an hour, and it did. He fell asleep with the window open and the smell of flowers in the air.

name: pool_cover_steps
does: Teaches you step by step how to put a cover on a pool or hot tub and where to store it, so the water stays clean for swim days and juicy picnics by the pool.
inputs: which pool or hot tub, and whether you are putting the cover on or taking it off
people say:
- How do I put the cover on the pool?
- Leaves keep falling in the water, what should I do?
- Help me fold the cover.
- Where should I put the cover in winter?
- I never know how to take the hot tub cover off.

Person: Could you make some tea, please?
Assistant: Happy to. How strong do you like it?
Person: Strong, please. My grandson's football team is coming over, and they all like it that way.
Assistant: Okay, strong tea. How many cups?
Person: Six. No, wait, seven. The coach is coming too.
Assistant: Seven cups, strong. The kettle does not seem to be plugged in. Can you plug it in?
Person: Done. Most days I only make one cup, you know.
Assistant: Then seven is a big day. I'll start the kettle now.

Someone wants a reminder to do something, like finish an audiobook.
Remind me at six.
Don't let me forget to call Mum tonight.
Ping me at eight to take my pills.
Tap me on the shoulder when it's time to leave for the bus.
Remind me to pick up the bright yellow jacket from the cleaner and to buy milk.
Let me know when it's half past four, I have to start dinner.
Remind me to return the audiobook to the library on Friday, and tell me again the day before.
Could you please remind me tomorrow morning to water the plants and to bring the blue folder to the meeting?

Someone wants to change a measurement from one unit to another.
How many cups is 500 ml?
5 miles in km?
Convert 70 degrees Fahrenheit to Celsius.
What's half a pound in grams?
I think my kitchen scale is wrong, how many ounces is two hundred grams?
I pay by the meter for fabric, so how many meters is ten yards?
How much is a stone in kilos?
Could you please tell me how many centimeters are in double the length of a foot? I am working at the bakery and the recipe tray is in different units.

A folder is like a drawer for the files on a computer. It keeps your work in one place so you can find it later. People change how files are sorted: they rename them, move them to another folder, or tag them with a color or a word. When the computer feels slow, people often restart it, because that clears out things that were left running. They say things like "Put this file in my work folder," "Tag this photo as holiday," or "Why is my laptop so slow? Restart it." The battery and the screen brightness are also easy to change when you ask.

Taras woke up and rubbed his eyes. He had not looked at his plans yet. "Good morning," he said to the phone. "Could you please search my calendar for a free hour this afternoon? I need to buy fuel and visit the garage about a new tire, and I don't want to miss any meetings." The phone searched and said he was free between two and three. Taras said, "Put a block there called car." The phone saved it. Then Taras got out of bed and went to make coffee, feeling ready for the day.

Someone wants to book a table at a restaurant tonight.
table for 2 tonight
book us a table at seven
any space at the pizza place on saturday?
reserve a table at the delicious thai place on main stret
i need a table with air conditioning, its too hot outside
book a table for ten on friday at six, i have to hide the plan from my wife
Could you please call the restaurant and ask if they have a table free tonight? It is my parents' anniversary.

Rodrigo moved to the city last month. His phone screen had a crack in it, and his bank account had very little money left. He asked his phone, "Could you please show me how much I spent this month on food and on my hobby? I am new here and I want to understand where my money goes, so I can plan better." The phone added up the numbers. It said he spent three hundred dollars on food and eighty on camera things. Rodrigo sighed, then asked it to set a monthly limit of two hundred and fifty for food.

The news on an assistant gives short headlines about the world, your town or sports. It is for people who want to know what is going on without reading a whole paper. People choose which topics they want, how many headlines to hear, and how often. They say things like "Read me the headlines," "Only sports, please," or "Don't read stories about celebrities." When a freezing storm is coming, many people ask for local news about the roads. Some people like the news in the morning, and others like a short summary at night.

It was a humid afternoon, and Giulia's phone battery was at nineteen percent. She was not good with phone settings. "My phone is nearly dead," she said. "I have a long train ride and no plan." The assistant said it could turn on battery saver and lower the screen brightness. Giulia said yes. It also offered to filter out noisy notifications by turning on do not disturb, and Giulia agreed. Now the phone would last through her ride. She thanked it and put the phone in her bag.

Once a month, Ravi baked bread for his neighbors. It was his monthly baking day, and he had to wait for the dough to rise. He did not want to blink and miss the oven time. He typed fast on his phone: "how lng do i bake the loaf at 200". The assistant said to bake it for thirty-five minutes at two hundred degrees. Ravi asked it to set a timer. Then he took a walk around the block while the bread baked. The timer rang when he got back, and the whole street smelled of fresh bread.

Someone wants the word count of their writing, and they can't wait to know.
Word count?
Count my words.
How long is this essay?
How many words so far?
How many words are in my essay about crispy fried chicken?
Is my draft about the kitchen shelf long enough?
Tell me how long my story is.
Could you please tell me how many words I have written today? I need to stay under five hundred.

Person: Good morning. I want to make pancakes.
Assistant: Good morning! How many pancakes do you want to make?
Person: Enough for four. No, six. My cousin is staying to watch a movie with us later.
Assistant: Six it is. Do you want the recipe now?
Person: Yes. And when are they done? Mine always look pale.
Assistant: Cook each side for about two minutes, until golden. Lift the edge with a spatula to check.
Person: Great. Can you also cook them for me?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't cook, but I can set a timer for each side.
Person: Okay, thanks.

Home security means keeping your house safe when you are home and when you are away. Cameras, alarms and motion sensors watch the doors and windows. People change when the alarm is on, who gets a message, and which cameras to look at. They say things like "Turn on the alarm," "Is the front door locked?" or "Show me the back garden." A good idea before a trip is to ask for the total number of open doors and windows. When the house is empty, many people switch the alarm to away mode.

A workout is a plan of exercises, with sets and reps. A rep is doing a move one time, and a set is a group of reps. Rest days give your muscles time to recover. People change how many sets they do, how heavy the weights are, and which days they train. They say things like "Add one more set," "Make today's workout shorter," or "Is tomorrow a rest day?" Many people train with a brother or a friend, even early when it is still dark. If you do not know a move, you can ask an assistant to explain it.

A podcast is a show with many episodes, and an audiobook is a book read aloud in chapters. The player remembers where you left off, so you can go on later. People change the speed, skip ahead, or go back a little. They say things like "Play it faster," "Go back thirty seconds," or "Pick up where I stopped." Some people listen while they clean the carpet, and others listen while they roast vegetables for dinner. A well made show is easy to follow, even at a faster speed.

Kwame was nervous. He had a video interview with a company in Tokyo, and he wanted to look his best. He fixed his tie in the mirror and asked his laptop, "What time is it in Tokyo now, and what time is it here when it is nine in the morning there?" The assistant said it was already evening in Tokyo, and that nine in the morning there would be midnight in Accra. Kwame pointed at his wall clock and laughed. The interview would be very late for him. He asked the assistant to set an alarm for eleven thirty at night, and it did.

Someone wants to know how long to cook something.
how long do i cook rice
cooking time for eggs?
how many minutes for a chicken in the oven
how long shuld i roast potatoes at 200
i want to win the bake-off, how long does the cake need
how long does popcorn take, i need a snack fast
Could you tell me how long to boil pasta? It is for our yearly family dinner and I do not want to ruin it.

Jonah, a grandfather, returned home from the shops on a hot day. The bedroom was freezing because the air conditioning had been on all morning, but the living room was warm. "Turn the air conditioning off in the bedroom and put the fan on in the living room," he said to the speaker. The speaker did both and said it would keep the fan on low. Outside, a van drove past, but inside the house it was quiet and fresh. Jonah sat down with a glass of water and enjoyed the cool air.

Delroy still kept the books for his son's shop. He had a bitter cup of tea beside him and a video call about to start. "Open the invoice from Monday and share my screen with the team," he said to his laptop. The laptop opened the invoice and put it on the shared screen, so everyone could see it. Delroy talked through the numbers, then thanked the team. After the call he said, "Thank you," to the laptop too, and it answered, "You're welcome." Delroy laughed and finished his tea.

Sanne came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. She had been working in the long flower bed all morning. "Book me a dentist appointment on Tuesday at ten," she told her phone. Then she looked out of the window and remembered she had a plant sale on Tuesday. "No, make it Wednesday," she said. The phone changed the booking to Wednesday at ten and asked if it should add it to her calendar. Sanne said yes. "Can you repeat the time?" she asked. The phone said, "Wednesday at ten in the morning."

After his morning jog, Mathieu, a retired teacher, wanted to bake his favorite lemon cake. He took care to ask for a recipe without nuts, because his friend was allergic. "Find me a lemon cake recipe, but I don't want nuts, and I don't want too much sugar," he said. The assistant found a simple recipe with no nuts and a little less sugar. It read the steps slowly, and Mathieu followed along. The cake needed forty minutes in the oven. He set a timer, and soon the kitchen smelled sweet.

Mathieu was nine years old and wanted to make a snack on his own. His jeans still had flour on them from last time. The kitchen door was closed so he would not wake his dad. He typed on the family tablet, in a hurry: "how do i make toast whith no mess". The assistant said to put the bread in the toaster, push the lever down, and wait until it pops up. It reminded him to ask an adult for help with hot things. A train went by outside while he waited, and the toast popped up golden.

name: write_and_send_email
does: Lets you email someone by saying what you want to tell them, then sends it after you say it looks good.
inputs: who to email, what to say, and any file to attach, like a black and white photo
people say:
- Tell Mrs Lee her hedge is growing over our fence.
- Write to my boss that I'm sick today.
- Send this photo to my sister.
- Let the school know Sam will be late tomorrow.
- Drop a quick note to the plumber.
